findings.finding: Large-cap Swedish industrial counterparties reported strong Q3 demand in the 48 hours before the print: Atlas Copco orders +25% organic, Sandvik orders +17% organic, SKF organic sales +4.3%, and the small technology trader OEM International orders +40% with 14% organic sales growth -- consistent with Indutrade's Process/Energy/Industrial companies converting the record Q2 backlog at or above the 4-5.5% organic growth brokers model.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Order/organic-growth surprises drive this name: Q3-2025 EBITA beat with orders hinting at recovery +8.2%; Q2-2026 record orders and EBITA +9% vs consensus +17.1%; Q1-2026 weak organic growth/EBITA -5.6% vs consensus -15.3% (Yahoo closes; Placera/Finwire reaction table).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the market sold these prints (Atlas Copco -7.2%, Sandvik -4%, OMXS30 -1.9% on 2026-10-22 intraday), and Indutrade fell 2.5% with them, so the read-across has not been bid into INDT; if it were, INDT would be outperforming its sector into the print rather than tracking the index down. Sized small because it is macro-to-company transmission from far larger, more cyclical businesses.
findings.independence: Sandvik Q3 (https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=bf64da489309d1515356c0c2d15f2be90&lang=en&src=listed), SKF Q3 (https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=b313f9ec58ee20a9c1b417e2c5788af47&lang=en&src=listed), OEM International Q3 (https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=b5d18eef63c53018e1e095b53e3c3e765&lang=en&src=listed) -- separate primary documents.

findings.finding: The closest business-model peers printed soft organic growth: Addtech (Jul-Sep) organic sales +2% with EBITA +17% flattered by a ~SEK 55m one-off in Safety (underlying ~+10%), and AddLife (life science, Indutrade's strongest Q2 area) organic +4%; Addtech fell ~3.4% on its report day.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same line as above: organic growth below expectations cost -15.3% (Q1-2026) and -6.2% / -5.9% (Q1/Q2-2025).
findings.why_not_priced: Addtech reported only this morning and INDT's -2.5% today is indistinguishable from the index's -1.9%, so no INDT-specific discount for a soft serial-acquirer organic print is visible; brokers' 4.2-5.5% organic estimates were set on 2026-10-08, before it. Sized small: Addtech is a narrower electrification/automation mix and Indutrade's Q2 organic orders (+8%) were well ahead of Addtech's.

findings.finding: Indutrade's own seasonality puts Q3 slightly above the bar: in 2025 the Q3 EBITA margin (14.6%) ran 0.9pp above Q2 (13.7%); applying that to Q2-2026's 14.7% on the ~SEK 8.8bn sales brokers model gives ~SEK 1,355-1,375m EBITA vs a 1,349-1,360m bar, with Nordea citing favourable FX.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EBITA vs consensus is the headline line: +9.4% beat -> +17.1% (Q2-26), -5.6% miss -> -15.3% (Q1-26), Q3-25 beat (1,143 vs 1,109) -> +8.2%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: brokers have the same seasonality and SB1 already models 15.3%; the residual is a ~1% EBITA edge, which on this name's ~1.7x elasticity to EBITA surprise is worth well under a point. If the market expected a clear beat, the stock would be holding its post-Q2 high (270.8 on 10-16) rather than giving back to 261.
